why_these_declarations_appeared_late: this file held six molecules and their toxicology verdicts from the day it was written, and no gate read it. The prohibition on candidate evidence in tools/verify_claims.py matched on two directory names and four marker strings, and this file sits under data/ with none of them, so it was never an admitted exception -- it was invisible. The rule is now structural: a file carrying a SMILES value is candidate evidence wherever it sits and under whatever name, and contracts/CANDIDATE_SHOWCASES.json admits this one as an input with its own field list, because an input carries identifiers and a verdict and not the derived chemistry its product carries. All three declarations were true of this file before they were written down; what changed is that something now fails if they are not.
what_this_is: the six candidate identifiers the appendix showcase is built from, with the structural-audit verdict each carried in the companion repository at the pinned commit. Nothing here is a measurement and nothing here is scored
why_the_verdicts_are_carried_rather_than: the audit's rule tables -- stability motifs, metabolic routes, liability families, chemotype signatures -- live in one place in the companion repository and are covered by its tests. Duplicating a SMARTS table into this repository would create two copies that can drift, and a drifted screen is worse than an absent one. So the verdict travels as pinned input with the commit that produced it, and this repository recomputes only what needs no rule table: canonical SMILES, InChIKey, formula, the bond graph, the topological pharmacophore and the stereocentres, all of which are RDKit primitives
selection_rule: of the 100 ESR1 records screened (the 25 lowest-numbered of each modality), the small molecules passing every hard clause of the audit -- identity fields reproduce, no stability alert, modality label supported by the structure, no undefined stereocentre -- ordered by ascending synthetic step proxy and then by identifier, first six taken. 44 of the 100 pass those clauses, and the rule re-derives the six from the identifiers alone
why_two_chemotypes_are_present: four of the six are triarylethylenes and two are quinazolinones, and that mixture is not curated -- it is what the ordering produced. It is worth seeing: the same triarylethylene signature the companion repository flags as WRONG under a FLT3 label is CORRECT here, because a tamoxifen-class skeleton belongs to a nuclear-receptor ligand-binding domain and not to a kinase hinge. One rule, one substructure, opposite verdicts by target
